challengeTypes: identify: India is located in which part of Asia? (South Asia vs East Asia vs West Asia vs Central Asia)

sort: Drag each fact about India's location to its correct description (India = in South Asia | Himalayas = in the north | Indian Ocean = to the south | Tropic of Cancer = passes through central India | India = extends from 8 degrees N to 37 degrees N latitude | India = extends from 68 degrees E to 97 degrees E longitude)
identify: Which country is India's neighbour to the NORTH? (China vs Sri Lanka vs Myanmar vs Maldives)

sort: Drag each neighbouring country to its correct direction (Pakistan = Northwest | China = North | Nepal = North | Bangladesh = East | Myanmar = East | Sri Lanka = South | Bhutan = Northeast | Afghanistan = Northwest)
identify: What are the FOUR main seasons in India? (Winter, Summer, Monsoon, Autumn vs Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter only | Hot, Cold, Wet, Dry | Morning, Noon, Evening, Night)

sort: Drag each season to its correct description (Winter = December to February, cold | Summer = March to May, hot | Monsoon = June to September, rainy | Autumn/Retreating monsoon = October to November, pleasant | Winter = cold and dry | Monsoon = southwest monsoon brings rain)
identify: Which type of natural vegetation is found in the Himalayan mountains? (Mountain forests with pine and deodar vs Mangroves vs Desert shrubs vs Tropical rainforests)

sort: Drag each vegetation type to its correct region (Tropical rainforest = areas with heavy rain like Western Ghats | Mountain forest = Himalayan region with pine and deodar | Desert vegetation = Rajasthan with thorny bushes | Mangrove forest = coastal areas like Sundarbans | Thorny scrub = dry regions | Deciduous forest = central India with trees that shed leaves)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) India location and extent — India is in South Asia. Extends from 8 degrees 4 minutes N to 37 degrees 6 minutes N latitude and 68 degrees 7 minutes E to 97 degrees 25 minutes E longitude. The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees N) passes through central India, dividing it into tropical and subtropical zones. Himalayas in the north, Indian Ocean in the south, Arabian Sea in the west, Bay of Bengal in the east. (2) India's neighbours — North: China, Nepal, Bhutan. Northwest: Pakistan, Afghanistan. East: Bangladesh, Myanmar. South: Sri Lanka, Maldives (island nations across the sea). India shares land borders with 7 countries. (3) Climate of India — Four main seasons: Winter (December-February, cold and dry), Summer (March-May, hot and dry), Monsoon/Southwest Monsoon (June-September, rainy), Autumn/Retreating Monsoon (October-November, pleasant). India has a monsoon climate — most rain comes from the southwest monsoon winds. (4) Natural vegetation — Tropical rainforests: areas with heavy rainfall (Western Ghats, Northeast India) — tall trees, dense canopy. Mountain forests: Himalayan region — pine, deodar, fir. Desert vegetation: Rajasthan — thorny bushes, cactus. Mangrove forests: coastal areas, deltas (Sundarbans) — trees that grow in salt water. Deciduous forests: central India — trees that shed leaves in dry season (teak, sal). Thorny scrub: dry regions. Misconceptions: 'India is in East Asia' (WRONG — India is in SOUTH Asia), 'India has only one neighbour' (WRONG — India has 7 land neighbours: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, plus Sri Lanka and Maldives across the sea), 'India has only three seasons like Europe' (WRONG — India has four main seasons including the monsoon which is unique to this region), 'the Tropic of Cancer passes through south India' (WRONG — the Tropic of Cancer passes through CENTRAL India, roughly through the middle of the country), 'all of India has the same vegetation' (WRONG — India has diverse vegetation: rainforests, mountain forests, deserts, mangroves, and deciduous forests depending on climate and rainfall).
